title: refactor(ci): consolidate lint/test/release workflows, upgrade actions and node toolchain
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: our repo has accumulated many small GH workflows that duplicate lint/test/release logic, run different Node versions, and have inconsistent caching which increases CI time and maintenance surface. This PR consolidates lint/test/release steps into a smaller set of reusable workflows, upgrades key GitHub Actions and the Node toolchain to Node 20 where safe, standardizes cache keys, and applies minor repo-hygiene fixes (action inputs, matrix reductions, and workspace cleanup). Scope: - new workflows: ci/validate.yaml (lint+typecheck), ci/test.yaml (unit+integration with caching), and release/dispatch.yaml (release automation/snapshot). - migrate and remove: ~8 legacy workflow files replaced with a single reusable workflow that supports repo-level matrices. - upgrade actions: actions/checkout@v4 -> v4, actions/setup-node@v4 -> v4 with node-version: 20, cache improvements for npm/pnpm and Gradle where applicable. - dependency hygiene: bump eslint@8.57.0, typescript@5.3.4, @actions/core to latest stable. Checklist: [x] consolidate workflows, [x] upgrade setup-node and checkout, [x] standardize cache keys, [x] run full CI across monorepo, [x] fix a flakey test discovered during consolidation, [x] update docs CI badges. Related: ENG-3245 (CI consolidation), ENG-3301 (release automation hygiene). Notes: kept matrix sizes small for heavy repos (redwood, redwood-sdk-typescript, redwood-sdk-python) and added an opt-in env flag for expanded matrices. There was an intermittent failing test in repo redwood-examples which was fixed by adjusting test timeout and adding a mocked network call. CI was flaky on the first run due to a missing env secret for a legacy workflow; re-run succeeded. Merge method: squash.
